Keys to the Hero:

* Broadly known as an "anti-carry" due to a skill that removes damage from enemies and transfers it to you, along with another ability that slows and damages anyone attacking you. This allows you to stand toe to toe with most enemies without issue for most of the game.  
* This hero is effective against melee opponents, especially in 1v1 lanes, as the damage transfer skill and early boots will help you win the lane. Also good against ranged heroes, but you become more reliant on a field ability and controlling runes for mana.  
* The damage transfer skill gives you damage even if you've drained all the attack damage from your enemy, so keep it going for as long as possible. You can also drain enemy illusions, so feel free to maximize the link off them.  
* The damage transfer skill and another ability both work if the hero goes invisible after using these skills. While a shadow blade isn't recommended, using an invisibility rune can be quite fun.  
* The damage transfer skill and the ultimate ability pierce magic immunity, so don't worry about items that grant it.  
* The main nuke ability is used to bully your enemies out of lane as well as speed up your farming. The energy field does damage twice, once outward and once back, with maximum damage when fully extended. Therefore, the key is to hit your enemies when it is at maximum distance, which becomes second nature once you get used to it. Bonus gold for farming creeps at the same time.  
* You tend to use all your skills very quickly, so this hero does exceptionally well against silence in all phases of the game.  
* The ultimate ability (without an upgrade) targets the lowest health enemy in range, and while the damage is important, don't underestimate the armor reduction per hit against enemy heroes.  
* This hero is one of the few in the game that can use a specific item to double the ultimate, which is awe-inspiring and strikes fear into all who oppose you.  
* The ultimate ability, when upgraded, targets towers and barracks over creeps and enemies, which quickly destroys these objectives.  
* An ability will trigger immediately when a specific hero charges you, so if you are paying attention, you will almost never get a surprise charge.  

Skills:

* Value point in the damage transfer skill, which is good for level 1 rune fights.  
* Max the ultimate ability and the main nuke when possible.  
* At least one value point in the slowing ability by level 4, likely prioritizing the damage transfer skill over it.  

Item Builds:

* There are two main ways to play this hero, and it doesn't change too much depending on the lane you are in (the main difference is that you likely won't need a bottle in the safelane). (1) Speedster or (2) Pushing.  
* The speedster (or fighting) build is the standard as it synergizes best with your kit, which relies on positioning (but not blink). Both the main nuke and the damage transfer skill require you to stay at a certain range from your enemy, so being faster than your opposition is helpful. This means choosing speed-enhancing boots over others. An efficient first item is a specific item, but consider another if there are many spells for early survivability and movement speed. A speed-enhancing item is also good to accelerate your movement speed and farming, with situational consideration for other items. Hint: the slow from one item is nice when using the damage transfer skill, and another is good to shed debuffs and push harder. Get a defensive item if needed, followed by an item that counters physical damage or one that counters magic/burst damage.  
* The more unconventional build is the pushing strategy. You will likely get a specific item and boots in this strategy. Many professionals will get a healing item, which is certainly useful at a good timing window. At this point, you really have to decide if you are committed to this strategy, and if you are, then you get an upgrade item and a specific item, though this can weigh your team down until each item is completed. A defensive item is necessary at any point. With the upgrade and two ultimates, you can take objectives very quickly, and basically no one can stop you or want to push into you. If they try, just use the damage transfer skill and attack them to death. Repeat every 60 seconds until the game is over.  
* Other items for consideration: A specific item is a great win-more/faster item for either build. An item that counters physical damage is an excellent choice if the game is hard and you need to deal with right-click damage from an enemy who can burst through the damage transfer skill, though another item works better in some situations. A specific armor item is also very good in some games since it fits the playstyle in either speedster or push mode. Other standard items to consider if the damage transfer skill isn't providing the damage your team needs include items that enhance critical hits or provide additional damage, though this hero isn't optimized to be a true scaling carry. Lastly, a specific item is now very useful in maximizing damage from the damage transfer skill and is a great counter to a specific ultimate.
